decisions.text: type stacked_bar: the totals compared, and roughly which parts dominate each: multiple stacked bars (G1.41)
the step 1,000 would leave 29% room above the data; 500 gives 0–3,500, 7 intervals, 13% room
the totals sorted by their size, descending (R7-20, G2.1)
stacking order from the base: Operations, HR, Finance, Outreach, PR, Development (the largest at the base, where it is read precisely; G7.31, D-26 (b))
each part in one colour and one place in every total: Operations (slot 1), HR (slot 2), Finance (slot 3), Outreach (slot 4), PR (slot 5), Development (slot 6) (G4.22, G7.31)
every name fits under its stacked bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart: vertical stacked bars
digits hidden: millions, stated once on the top label (R2-05, D-3): “$3.5 million in expenses”

each stack's total labelled at its end, the totals being the message: East 3.1, Central 2.6, West 2.5, in the scale's magnitude and form, its top label giving the unit (G1.41, G7.4; owner, 1 Oct 2026)
the unit phrase on the top label: “$3.5 million in expenses”; the top gridline starts after it

each part named beside the last stack, level with the middle of its segment, top to bottom as stacked: Development, PR, Outreach, Finance, HR, Operations; thin leaders to Development, moved off their segments to clear the others (G5.4, D-31 (c))
the title wraps onto two lines
